# Legacy compact reachability check, official 0.158.0

The supported OpenAI compaction path in the pinned official client is Responses
V2. Disabling `remote_compaction_v2` cannot restore `/responses/compact`: the key
is removed and its configured boolean is explicitly ignored.

This follow-up ran the same verified official binary once with
`-c features.remote_compaction_v2=false`, the previous synthetic OAuth bootstrap,
the local custom-CA HTTPS mock, and `--network none`. It exited 0 and emitted
three POST requests, all to `/backend-api/codex/responses`. The middle request
contains `compaction_trigger` and metadata `request_kind: compaction`. Even with
the explicit false setting, its beta header still contains
`remote_compaction_v2`. The exact invocation and complete request index are saved.

No HTTP request was generated by the harness. The mock's ability to reply to a
legacy path is not evidence that any client visited it; the observed legacy
request count is zero. The actual compaction request saved here was emitted by
the unmodified official binary.

The old generic telemetry comment mentioning a Compact endpoint in
`core/src/client.rs:856` does not define a callable endpoint. The concrete
capability and dispatch code above establishes the supported behavior.

## Actual compact encoding and header sequence

The new flag-off compaction request uses **zstd**, exactly as the previous V2
capture. Its single frame begins `28b52ffd0058`, has a 2 MiB window, no content-size
field, no dictionary and no checksum. The saved compressed body was independently
decoded with the host zstd CLI and matched `compact.decoded.json` exactly.

Header order, read directly from `compact.headers.raw`:

```text
version
x-codex-beta-features
x-codex-window-id
x-codex-turn-metadata
x-codex-routing-hint
x-client-request-id
session-id
thread-id
accept
content-encoding
content-type
authorization
chatgpt-account-id
originator
user-agent
host
content-length
```

This sequence equals the previous V2 compaction sequence; it is not a separate
legacy compact sequence. The pinned client supplies no reachable supported legacy
request from which a legacy encoding or header order can be measured. Do not
relabel this request as `/responses/compact`, and do not invent an identity or
zstd rule for that distinct endpoint from these data.

`result.json` records the conclusion, hashes and boundaries. Only the new
flag-off run metadata and its one compaction request/reply are added here;
earlier standard/Lite/TLS captures are preserved and not duplicated. This
custom-CA HTTP observation does not add native TLS evidence.
